findings.conclusion: Both cached MCP package manifests and both cached coreBundle.js files are byte-identical. The implementation actually inspected is playwright-core, called by the thin @playwright/mcp CLI wrapper. Which cached copy the existing process loaded remains outside this worker scope.

With no server port, MCP transport is stdio. Server startup/initialize and an initial tools/list do not create a browser backend. First tools/call lazily creates it. An already pending backendPromise is also awaited by later tools/list, so catalogue availability is not browser connection proof and later catalogue requests can wait on that promise.

For --extension, first-call backend creation follows initializeServer -> factory.create -> createBrowserWithInfo -> createBrowser -> createExtensionBrowser. Extension attachment occurs before BrowserBackend.callTool dispatches browser_tabs. Thus the first browser_tabs timeout can be in backend connection even before the tabs handler executes.

browser_tabs list is not a passive transport health check: its handler awaits ensureTab; ensureTab initializes context, creates a new tab if none exists, can close/reset a crashed current tab, and waits for tab initialization. First call can also open the extension connect page through the browser executable.

Expected Playwright Extension ID is mmlmfjhmonkocbjadbfplnigmagldckm. Supplied --browser msedge chooses Edge, and explicit --profile-dir-name Default wins over automatic last-used extension-profile discovery. On Windows the standard msedge user data path is LOCALAPPDATA/Microsoft/Edge/User Data, subject to custom path/executable overrides that this worker did not read.

Before relay creation, the default executable/profile path checks extension installation by existence of Extensions/<id>, or a nonempty extensions.settings[<id>] record in Preferences or Secure Preferences. This predicate does not establish extension enabled state, protocol compatibility, user approval, selected tabs, or live handshake. Missing installation normally throws a specific Extension not found error before relay startup; executable-path override bypasses that standard-path check.

The relay listens on an ephemeral port with default hostname localhost. It accepts only random /extension/<uuid> and /cdp/<uuid> WebSocket upgrade paths. There is no health/status HTTP route in this relay: allowed-host ordinary HTTP requests return 404; disallowed Host returns 403. Do not infer extension readiness from a listening socket or HTTP response.

Connect-page launch uses chrome-extension://<Playwright ID>/connect.html with relay URL, MCP client metadata, protocolVersion=2, and optional token. It spawns the chosen browser executable with the configured profile directory (windowsHide, detached, no shell). Handshake needs both an incoming extension WebSocket and extension.initialized; merely having an Edge window or extension files does not satisfy it.

The extension-connect deadline is default 30 seconds only when PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXTENSION_TOKEN is truthy. Without a token the deadline is 0, and raceAgainstDeadline installs no timeout. After handshake, relay connectOverCDP is invoked with timeout=0; extension request callbacks also contain no per-request timer. These are source-supported ways a first tool call may reach an outer 120-second deadline. Actual token presence/value and precise blocked stage were not inspected; no root cause is established.

In the inspected MCP call path, extra.signal reaches backend.callTool only after backendPromise resolves; initializeServer/factory.create receive no request signal. Therefore outer tool timeout alone cannot be treated as proof that a pending extension handshake was canceled, relay closed, or owned resources released. Actual process/socket lifecycle needs separate existing-state evidence.

Protocol v2 forwards extension events for tabs/debugger plus extension.initialized. After initialization Playwright connects to the local CDP relay and auto-attaches known tabs using the extension. Duplicate extension/CDP clients, malformed messages, disconnects, extension RPC errors and missing executable/profile have distinct code paths; the generic earlier outer timeout identifies none of them by itself.

This installed package identifies a Microsoft Playwright Extension and its exact ID. It is a separate connection path from the parent's OpenAI Computer Use extension. Computer Use window enumeration or its local-browser setting does not prove this Playwright handshake. This investigation supplies no authorization or method to bypass the existing Computer Use URL-policy stop.

This server registers tools/list and tools/call with tools-only capability; it has no resources/list handler or fallback. For an already-connected server, the bundled MCP SDK sends JSON-RPC -32601 Method not found for resources/list without entering factory.create or browser initialization. A host-side list_mcp_resources helper might reject locally or lazily start its MCP transport; those helper behaviors were not inspected. Only a demonstrated server round-trip establishes current MCP responsiveness, and it still does not establish browser readiness.

The actual installed Edge Default extension manifest identifies Playwright Extension version 0.4.0, Manifest V3, with lib/background.mjs service worker and debugger/activeTab/tabs/tabGroups permissions. Its connect UI requires protocol 2 exactly; installed MCP defaults to protocol 2. This explicit protocol gate matches. No mismatch or basis for reinstall/update was found in this comparison; current enabled state and live interoperability are not proven.

After validating the loopback URL and protocol version, connect UI records connectionRequested. A matching token automatically calls handleConnectToTab; a nonempty mismatching token shows Invalid token provided. Without a token the UI lists candidate tabs with the exact button label Allow & select. connectionRequested only stores the relay URL; connectToTab later takes that record and opens WebSocket (5-second open timeout). ConnectedTabGroup sends the selected tab event and extension.initialized. Therefore waiting for user tab selection is a source-supported possible stall; no current/historical UI state was inspected and no actual token was read.

Connect-page action label is Allow & select; success text is client-name connected. Status-page labels are Connected to, Accessible page:/Accessible pages:, Disconnect, and No clients are currently connected... . Status page queries getConnectionStatus from the service worker; no HTTP health endpoint is added by these pages. The connect UI states that allowing connection exposes the browser and may permit later reconnects, so the tab selection is a session authorization/mutation, not a passive diagnostic read. No UI action was taken, and the Computer Use URL-policy boundary remains in force.
